# Neural Reality Capture Skill for Muse

A provider-independent craft guide for neural reality capture: turning photographed or video-derived real places, objects, aerial sites, interiors, or people into photogrammetric meshes, NeRFs, or 3D Gaussian splats. It helps choose the right representation from the final use (editable mesh vs novel-view NeRF vs real-time splat), then walks through capture planning (overlap, exposure discipline, loops vs panoramas, scale strategy), calibration, reconstruction/training, cleanup, compression and LOD, coordinate and interchange handoff (glTF/GLB, USD), visual/geometric QA, archival records, and property, location, people, and cultural rights checks — with evidence labels separating paper facts, standard facts, official documentation, empirical observations, and production heuristics. Discovered via skills.sh. Honest note: this is production craft, not auto-execution — you need capture tooling (COLMAP-class software or a capture service) and hundreds of well-shot overlapping photos; it explicitly refuses metrology promises without surveyed control; and it won't invent subjects (no text-to-3D). skills.sh Trust Hub: unverified. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
